as_told.title: Norton AFB meeting: Air Force asks Emenegger and Sandler to make a UFO documentary
as_told.place_text: Norton Air Force Base, California; the Pentagon

plain: In the early 1970s, the story goes, US military officials asked two documentary makers, Allan Sandler and Robert Emenegger, to make a film about UFOs, and offered them real military footage for it. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says two officials approached them and said they could use footage from Holloman, an Air Force base, in which a craft is said to land. Michels, in his own framing, says Emenegger was in touch with Norton Air Force Base and that when he went there "everybody there is talking to him about UFOs." He ties this to their film UFOs: Past, Present and Future, and mentions the astronomer J. Allen Hynek and the television writer Rod Serling. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron, passing on what Emenegger told him, puts the meeting at Norton around 1973 rather than 1971. He names a man named Paul Shartle, a Colonel Coleman, and H.R. Haldeman, a senior aide in the White House, and says the officials asked for "this other documentary on UFOs, but we'd like you to hide it below the other eight documentaries." If it is true, the military wanted to release UFO material to the public quietly, through filmmakers.
